actions.label: Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
Have FWB staff directly manage and supervise food disbursement
Hand food stocks over to the guard structures for distribution
Allow FWB staff to move freely inside the camp without escort
Provide an ongoing, scheduled food supply to the camp's refugees
Permit FWB to document and publicly report within security limits
Consult refugees directly on their aid needs during distribution

goals.label: FWB staff move freely inside the camp without escort
Camp infrastructure (generators, fuel, sewage, shelter) is funded and running
Host town economy and goodwill, with local actors prioritized
The camp receives a sufficient, ongoing food supply
Accountability and documentation of aid recipients for donors
Burdensome external assessments and procedures in the camp
Commander and militia control food distribution and camp operations
FWB controls the distribution process independently
FWB's neutrality and independence as a humanitarian actor
Food aid is diverted or skimmed by guards, militia or officials
Food is distributed fairly to all refugees without discrimination
Food is used to coerce, abuse or collectively punish refugees
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Guards rebel, lose discipline or resent refugees' better rations
Hostile actors exploit outside access or aid to gain resources or attack
Public visibility and reputation of FWB's work and camp conditions
Refugees actually receive adequate food aid
Refugees stay contained in the camp and do not reach the capital
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants
Senior Militia Leader's trust in and backing of the commander
Visible abuse or unrest draws international attention and political or legal costs
Accurate information on refugees' nutritional needs
Refugees have a say in what aid they need

redLines.label: Permit FWB to hire local assistants for distribution, prioritising local workers
redLines.quote: FWB's hiring of local independent laborers for the food distribution is a sufficient condition for you being unable to trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Hire FWB-chosen local assistants from the host community for distribution
redLines.quote: FWB's hiring of local independent laborers for the food distribution is a sufficient condition for you being unable to trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
